current_text.html: The only parties entitled to an appeal are those who have submitted to a regular trial, those appealing a censure in a BCO 38-1 case without process, those appealing the elevation of a censure under BCO 36-8, and those appealing a BCO 34-10 divestiture without censure.

relationships.title: Seven overtures held over from the 48th to 49th General Assembly
relationships.disposition: not in conflict (all seven); Adopted by the CCB

metadata.summary: CCB advised that all seven overtures carried over from the 48th GA, touching discipline, appeals, and related BCO provisions, are not in conflict with the Constitution.

relationships.title: Appealing a censure imposed without formal judicial process

metadata.summary: An overture amending BCO 38-1 and 42-2 to allow appeal of a censure in cases conducted without formal process was found not in conflict and adopted.

relationships.title: Confession timing requirements in cases without process

metadata.summary: The CCB found that amending BCO 38-1 regarding timing of confession in cases without process was not in conflict with the BCO, and the overture was adopted.

relationships.title: Mandating That Those Without Call Report Annually to Presbytery

metadata.summary: An overture mandating annual presbytery reporting for officers without call was in conflict with the Constitution because the new BCO 34-10 language conflicted with BCO 42-2.

relationships.title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: Since the complainant did not appear for a trial, he does not have the right to appeal (BCO 42-2).

metadata.synopsis: After a Session excommunicated a member without trial for contumacy, the SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the contumacy judgment, excommunication, and later Session and Presbytery actions. No mutually agreed BCO 38-1 confession existed, and declining a confession meeting was not immediately censurable objective contumacy under BCO 32-6; subjective contumacy required confession or trial. He reverted to membership under pending indictment. The SJC did not find the indictment unconstitutional, decide trial guilt, or consider the unpleaded trespass warning.

relationships.title: Spann v. Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church

metadata.synopsis: An individual appealed directly to the SJC, alleging her church effectively excommunicated her without process, failed the Matthew 18 process, and spiritually abused her by social isolation. The SJC dismissed as premature, without reaching the merits, because there was no record of a judicial decision by the church or of an appeal to Evangel Presbytery, the next higher court; it stated she could proceed only by providing such evidence. The severity of excommunication did not excuse that prerequisite. The SJC asked Presbytery to obtain the session's written response to her letter.

relationships.title: McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: 2. The Appeal is Judicially Out of Order because "only those who have submitted to a regular trial are entitled to an Appeal" (BCO 42-2).

metadata.synopsis: An appellant under suspension from the sacraments challenged the presbytery's judicial commission process and censure. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order—not decided on the merits—because he had not submitted to a regular trial, as BCO 42-2 requires. Treated as a complaint, it was also out of order: it had not first been presented to the presbytery, and the 30-day period had expired. The SJC further barred complaints about later court actions while he remained under censure, except as to the highest censure. The censure stood.

relationships.title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Nashville Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of reports against TE George Grant was inadequately documented and internally inconsistent, and the evidence before Presbytery raised a strong presumption of guilt, the SJC held. It sustained the complaint, ruling that pastoral reconciliation does not displace the duty to institute judicial process, and remanded for further proceedings; it did not adjudicate Grant guilty. A concurrence agreed only in remanding to supplement the record under BCO 42-5 & 7.

relationships.title: Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Chastain appealed Heritage Presbytery’s 2006 excommunication and deposition. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order because Chastain had renounced PCA jurisdiction on May 8, 2006. Consequently, Presbytery’s later proceedings were moot and SJC 2005-1 remained in effect. The SJC did not reach the merits. A concurrence questioned the discipline process after renunciation; a dissent argued the majority lacked constitutional authority to recognize unilateral withdrawal and thereby undercut discipline.

relationships.title: Aureliano Tan Jr. v. Houston Metro Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: This case was found judicially out of order in that the appellant did not submit to a regular trial as required by BCO 42-2.

metadata.synopsis: Tan attempted to appeal without first submitting to a regular trial. The SJC found the appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 and therefore did not reach its merits. Although the source header labels the disposition “dismissed,” the adopted judgment expressly classifies it as judicially out of order.

relationships.title: Jerguson v. Western Carolina

occurrences.excerpt: on the basis of BCO 42-2. The case is not ready for higher court review

metadata.synopsis: The SJC held Jerguson’s appeal judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 because Western Carolina Presbytery was rehearing the case. The matter therefore was not ready for higher-court review. The decision did not reach the merits or dismiss the underlying Presbytery proceedings.

relationships.title: Nancy J. Plowman v. Philadelphia Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: BCO 42-2 states that a ground for an appeal is the "manifestation of prejudice.

metadata.synopsis: A member suspended from the Lord's Table appealed after Presbytery let the Session resume her trial and failed to lift all suspensions. The SJC sustained the appeal, finding the Session's premature censure, truncated trial, and prosecutor-judge conflict manifested prejudice and made a fair trial impossible. It set aside all judgments and censures, treated the November 13, 2003 communion letter as non-censuring advice, and did not remand.

relationships.title: Paul W. Lee v. Korean Southwest

metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed three convictions and suspension that would automatically become indefinite absent repentance. The SJC sustained the appeal: unauthorized committee citations and admonition without process could not support guilt, and multiple trial violations were fatally prejudicial. It set aside the judgment, dismissed the citation and admonition charges, and revoked both censures. The inappropriate-language charge was not adjudicated on its merits; Presbytery could retry it on remand or dismiss it.

relationships.title: Mark Herzor and Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Case 2002-18 is a complaint (the heading also says "Reference") identified in the adopted motion as TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery. The SJC found it judicially out of order because it was filed against actions of a judicial commission, not completed Presbytery actions (BCO 15-3, 43-1). The full SJC approved that action on October 16, 2003. No merits ruling or later dismissal is stated; the Manual only outlines a possible dismissal route.

metadata.synopsis: A church session suspended a member from the Lord's Table and found her guilty of contumacy. The chairman of Presbytery's Judicial Business Committee advised her that her appeal was out of order; Presbytery later ruled her complaint untimely. The SJC sustained her complaint: she had submitted to regular trial, making her appeal in order under BCO 42-2, and her complaint was timely after Presbytery's advice caused the appeal to be renamed. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the appeal. Filing the appeal suspended the Lord's Table censure pending final adjudication; the SJC questioned the contumacy ruling.

relationships.title: Sung K. Kim v. Korean Capital Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …("Only those who have submitted to a regular trial are entitled to an Appeal" BCO 42-2). Mr. Kim did not submit to a regular trial before Korean Capital Presbytery, was found guilty of contumacy by the Presbytery, and was deposed from office (BCO 34-4).

metadata.synopsis: TE Sung K. Kim appealed his deposition by Korean Capital Presbytery, but the SJC declared the appeal judicially out of order. Because Kim had not submitted to a regular trial, he was not entitled to appeal under BCO 42-2; the Presbytery had instead found him guilty of contumacy and deposed him from office under BCO 34-4. The ruling disposes of the appeal without reaching its merits and leaves the deposition in force.

relationships.title: Mark Chavalas v. Northern Illinois Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …prior to the resignation of Dr. Chavalas, who did submit to a regular trial (BCO 42-2).

metadata.synopsis: Chavalas appealed a Northern Illinois Presbytery judgment, but testimony cited by both parties was missing from the record. Because recording-machine failures made the required transcripts unavailable and Presbytery could not cure the defect, the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order, dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7. Chavalas’s later resignation did not abandon the appeal because he had appealed beforehand after a regular trial; no rebuke was issued.

relationships.title: Ed Fitzsimmons v. Evangel Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: The SJC refused to hear Ed Fitzsimmons's appeal from Evangel Presbytery because his appeal was not filed with the General Assembly's Stated Clerk within the 30-day deadline of BCO 42-2. The appeal was declared administratively out of order, and no merits question was decided. The sparse record shows a straightforward application of the filing deadline; it does not disclose the underlying presbytery action or any merits view.

relationships.title: Raymond Larsen v. Pacific Presbytery (Appeal)

occurrences.excerpt: …contumacy with regard to his failure to appear for trial on February 1, 1997. BCO 42-2 provides that 'Only those who have submitted to regular trial are entitled to an appeal."

metadata.synopsis: Raymond Larsen sought to appeal a Session judgment deposing him for contumacy after he failed to appear for trial. The SJC unanimously found the appeal administratively out of order because BCO 42-2 permits an appeal only by a person who submitted to a regular trial. The notice does not review the merits of the deposition.

relationships.title: Session of Harvestwood PCA v. New River Presbytery (Complaint)

metadata.synopsis: New River Presbytery treated Grace Covenant PCA's BCO 41 inquiry about a Sunday school teacher's acceptability as a request for advice, but then ruled he was eligible to teach. On Harvestwood's complaint, the SJC held that Presbytery lacked original jurisdiction to make that final disposition and that the record was unclear about the teacher's views. The SJC sustained the complaint and recommended that Presbytery rescind its March 15, 1997 action and clarify his views through proper BCO procedures; it declined to reach the creation and theistic-evolution merits.

The SJC found the appeal in order (17-4) and remanded the case for retrial (21-0) on grounds that the Judicial Commission committed significant procedural errors, including abandoning original charges and convicting Clark of contumacy on new charges without giving him opportunity to respond.

relationships.title: Clark v. Southwest Presbytery (Request for Clarification)

metadata.synopsis: John P. Clark, Jr. requested clarification of the SJC decision in Case 93-5 regarding who controls the assets of South Valley Presbyterian Church, Inc. after the congregation voted to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC held it lacked jurisdiction over the civil corporate entity and its property, declining to rule on Clark's request.

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church complained against New River Presbytery's action sustaining a complaint that a Sunday school teacher holding theistic evolution and other doctrinal exceptions should not teach. The SJC partially sustained the complaint, declining to refer the matter back to the church with instructions but advising that the teacher should not teach while he holds exceptions that could require him to teach contrary to the fundamentals of the system of doctrine.
